newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas drifts lower ahead of cooler air.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas drifts lower ahead of cooler air.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices drifted lower Monday in anticipation of cooler weather Tuesday throughout most of the East and Midwest, market sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, physical prices slipped an average of three cents to $2.17-2.22 per mmBtu at Henry Hub, with the bulk of the deals reported done at the lower end of the range.
In the Midwest, prices also softened ahead of the cooler weather to about $2.08-2.12.
Early August values in the Midcontinent were quoted at $2.00-2.04, which would indicate a gain of only a couple of cents from most July indices.
Similarly in the Permian Basin market, prices for Tuesday delivery slipped two cents to about $2.12-2.13.
San Juan prices held around $2.09-2.10 as California demand remained fairly strong.

Separately, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico was back on line following a brief weekend outage. The adjacent unit 5, also rated at 750 MW, was still expected to restart next week.
In the East, despite an expected 10-degree drop in temperatures overnight, swing gas at the New York city gate was quoted at $2.38-2.45.
